meta.purpose: Five events, defined before any code ships, so that 'which page works' becomes a question with an answer.
meta.status: Self-hosted counter implemented. Static GitHub Pages does not receive events.
principles: first-party only: the collector must live on the site's own host, not a third party
No cookie, fingerprint or session identifier; visits are not eligible sessions.
aggregate only: no per-visitor record is stored, so the data cannot be joined to a person
no Amazon data: nothing about what happens after the click is knowable from this site, and nothing is implied
meta.explicitly_out_of_scope: Reported orders, revenue and conversion rate. Those can only come from the Associates dashboard or the API, which this session cannot read. The campaign ledger starts empty and stays empty until authorised first-party reports exist.

events.name: page_view
events.fires_when: A guide, category or register page is rendered
events.answers: Which pages are reached at all, and from where

events.name: outbound_product_click
events.fires_when: A reader activates an outbound link to a product listing
events.answers: Which products and which positions earn the click
not_collected: anything after the click; the destination is Amazon's, not ours
events.note: The click is counted locally before navigation. It does not prove a purchase, a session, or a commission.

events.name: guide_read_75
events.fires_when: A reader reaches 75% of a guide's height
events.answers: Whether the guide is actually read or merely opened
not_collected: time per paragraph, scroll path, mouse movement

events.name: compare_view
events.fires_when: The comparison page or a comparison table is rendered
events.answers: Whether readers want side-by-side data more than prose
not_collected: individually identifying data of any kind

events.name: flag_page_view
events.fires_when: The Flagged for Review page is opened
events.answers: Whether the review page is actually consulted, which tells us if the verification work is visible

collector_design.payload: Event name, allowlisted publication page, and optional observed ASIN. Daily aggregate counts only.
collector_design.retention: aggregate counts per day per event per prop value; raw events discarded on write
collector_design.opt_out: Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control headers must be honoured by skipping the send
collector_design.why_not_deployed: Deploying it requires a host that can run a process. GitHub Pages serves static files only, so there is nowhere for the collector to run. A third-party analytics provider would meet the measurement goal but would break the first-party principle and add a disclosure obligation that is not worth it before there is traffic to measure.

rules: a row is added only when the figure comes from an authorised first-party report
every row carries the date the figure was pulled and the report it came from
no projection, no forecast, no model output is permitted in this table
reported_orders is left blank until the Associates report provides it
